extracted.intended_audience: community water system operators, water utility compliance staff, and State drinking water regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and criteria for conducting Initial Distribution System Evaluations (IDSE), standard monitoring or system-specific studies, and subpart V compliance monitoring (TTHM and HAA5) including turbidity/filtration monitoring and reporting/recordkeeping obligations under EPA Part 141 subparts T, U, and V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration demonstration requirements (non-standard filtration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use filtration other than slow sand, diatomaceous earth, conventional, or direct filtration you must conduct a demonstration (pilot plant studies or other means) that your filtration combined with disinfection consistently achieves specified removal/inactivation levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System must demonstrate: 99% removal of Cryptosporidium oocysts; 99.9% removal and/or inactivation of Giardia lamblia cysts; and 99.99% removal and/or inactivation of viruses. Use pilot plant studies or other means acceptable to the State (see tables in §141.551).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lime softening — combined filter effluent sample acidification
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems practicing lime softening may acidify representative combined filter effluent (CFE) turbidity samples prior to analysis using a State-approved protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires approval by the State for the acidification protocol used on representative CFE turbidity samples; applies to combined filter effluent sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of individual filter turbidity monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H systems serving fewer than 10,000 people and utilizing conventional filtration or direct filtration must conduct continuous turbidity monitoring for each individual filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a requirement for qualifying systems (subpart H, <10,000 population, conventional/direct filtration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous turbidity monitoring method and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous monitoring must use an approved method, have calibration per manufacturer procedures, record results at least every 15 minutes, meet monthly reporting requirements, and maintain records per §141.571.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: use an approved method in §141.74(a); calibrate turbidimeters per manufacturer; record results at least every 15 minutes; report monthly per §141.570; retain records per §141.571.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidimeter failure contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: If continuous turbidity monitoring equipment fails, the system must conduct grab sampling every four hours until the turbidimeter is back online and has 14 days to resume continuous monitoring before a violation is incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grab sampling every 4 hours replaces continuous monitoring during failure period; 14-day grace period to resume continuous monitoring; after 14 days a violation is incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-or-fewer filters alternative monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system has two or fewer filters, it may conduct continuous monitoring of combined filter effluent (CFE) instead of individual filter effluent monitoring, subject to same monitoring/calibration/reporting/recordkeeping requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring of CFE must meet the same requirements in §141.560(a)–(d) and §141.561 as individual filter monitoring; when assessing or triggering actions, treat CFE as applicable to both filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement for 1.0 NTU exceedance (two consecutive readings)
rubrics_metrics.description: If turbidity of an individual filter (or CFE for 2-filter systems monitoring CFE) exceeds 1.0 NTU in two consecutive recordings 15 minutes apart, report to the State by the 10th of the following month with filter number(s), date(s), turbidity value(s) and cause if known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reporting (by the 10th) must include identification of filter(s), dates and values of exceedances, and known cause(s). Applies when two consecutive 15-minute readings exceed 1.0 NTU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-assessment trigger for repeated 1.0 NTU exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: If for three months in a row turbidity exceeded 1.0 NTU in two consecutive 15-minute recordings at the same filter (or CFE for 2-filter CFE-monitoring systems), conduct a self-assessment within 14 days of the triggering exceedance unless a CPE was required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-assessment must include at least: assessment of filter performance; development of a filter profile; identification and prioritization of factors limiting filter performance; assessment of applicability of corrections; and preparation of a filter self-assessment report. Systems with 2 filters monitoring CFE must self-assess both filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Performance Evaluation (CPE) trigger for repeated 2.0 NTU exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: If for two months in a row turbidity exceeded 2.0 NTU in two consecutive 15-minute recordings at the same filter (or CFE for 2-filter CFE-monitoring systems), arrange a CPE by the State or a State-approved third party no later than 60 days after the trigger; if conducted, submit completed CPE within 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: if a CPE was completed within prior 12 months or the system/State are in an ongoing CTA project, a new CPE may not be required. If a required CPE is conducted it must be completed and submitted to the State no later than 120 days following the trigger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lime softening — alternative turbidity exceedance levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems using lime softening may apply to the State for alternative turbidity exceedance levels, provided they demonstrate higher turbidity levels are due to lime carryover only and not degraded filter performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application to State must demonstrate cause (lime carryover) and show that elevated turbidity is not from filter degradation to obtain alternate exceedance levels for the §141.563 table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly reporting items — combined filter effluent
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems subject to combined filter effluent requirements must report monthly (by the 10th) the total number of filtered water turbidity measurements, the number and percentage ≤ the system's required 95th percentile limit, and the date/value of any turbidity measurements exceeding the system's maximum turbidity value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All these items are due by the 10th of the following month for combined filter effluent (CFE) monitoring (see §§141.550–141.553).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly reporting items — individual filter turbidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly reporting (by the 10th) must include that the system conducted individual filter turbidity monitoring, filter number(s)/date(s)/turbidity value(s) that exceeded 1.0 NTU for 2 consecutive measurements, self-assessment trigger/completion dates (timing exception if triggered in last 4 days), CPE trigger/date if required, and a copy of completed CPE report within 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting schedule: by the 10th of following month for most items; self-assessment completion can be reported within 14 days if the trigger occurred during the last four days of the month; completed CPE report must be submitted within 120 days after trigger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting items — disinfection profiling and benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Disinfection profiling reporting: report results of optional monitoring showing low DBP levels or that the system has begun disinfection profiling (timing varies by system size). Disinfection benchmarking reporting: anytime considering a significant change to disinfection, submit description of proposed change, disinfection profile (for Giardia and, if necessary, viruses), disinfection benchmark, and analysis of effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiling: report optional monitoring results demonstrating TTHM <0.064 mg/L and HAA5 <0.048 mg/L (or that profiling has begun) by specified deadlines depending on system population. Benchmarking: submit proposed change description and analysis whenever considering significant disinfection changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping durations for turbidity and disinfection records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of individual filter monitoring results for at least 3 years; retain disinfection profiling results and raw data and analysis indefinitely; retain disinfection benchmarking benchmark and raw data and analysis indefinitely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping per §141.571: (a) individual filter monitoring results — ≥3 years; (b) disinfection profiling results (including raw data/analysis) — indefinitely; (c) disinfection benchmarking (including raw data/analysis) — indefinitely.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDSE purpose and use
rubrics_metrics.description: An Initial Distribution System Evaluation (IDSE) must be used to determine locations with representative high TTHM and HAA5 concentrations throughout the distribution system to identify subpart V compliance monitoring locations (used in conjunction with subpart L compliance monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDSE is separate from subpart L compliance monitoring and is used to select subpart V monitoring locations; results are not to be used for MCL compliance determinations (§141.600(a), (f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDSE applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: You are subject to IDSE requirements if you are a community water system using a primary or residual disinfectant other than ultraviolet light (or deliver water so treated), or a nontransient noncommunity water system serving at least 10,000 people using such disinfectants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability defines which systems must perform IDSE and related subpart V activities (see §141.600(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDSE compliance schedule and State review timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must comply with IDSE submission/completion schedules based on population category (table). If the State does not approve or notify within specified timeframes after submission, the plan/report may be considered approved and must be implemented; State may adjust combined distribution system inclusion based on certain factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedules specified in §141.600(c) include different submission and completion dates by population. Notes: if State does not act within 12 months on a plan it may be considered approved; State may exclude some wholesale/consecutive systems from combined distribution systems under certain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDSE compliance pathway options
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet IDSE requirements you must conduct standard monitoring (§141.601), or a system specific study (§141.602), or certify to the State that you meet 40/30 certification criteria (§141.603), or qualify for a very small system waiver (§141.604).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven't taken required samples for 40/30 eligibility, you must conduct standard monitoring or a system specific study. Choice of pathway depends on prior monitoring, system size, and other criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methods requirement for IDSE and studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only the analytical methods specified in §141.131 or otherwise approved by EPA for monitoring under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All TTHM and HAA5 samples for compliance, IDSE, standard monitoring, or system specific studies must use methods in §141.131 or EPA-approved alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard monitoring plan required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard monitoring plan must include a schematic of the distribution system (entry points and sources and storage facilities) with projected monitoring locations and dates, justification of monitoring location selection with summary of data relied on, specification of population served and system type, and retention of the submitted plan (including State modifications) for the IDSE report retention period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a complete copy of the plan and any State modifications for as long as IDSE reports must be retained under §141.601(a)(4). Submit the plan to the State per the IDSE schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard monitoring sample set and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard monitoring requires dual sample sets at each monitoring location (one sample for TTHM and one for HAA5) during one monitoring period in the peak historical month for TTHM/HAA5 or warmest water temperature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review available compliance/study/operational data to determine the peak historical month. Dual sample set definition: a TTHM and an HAA5 sample taken at each location during each monitoring period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard monitoring location counts and frequencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard monitoring must follow the table specifying number of monitoring periods, frequency, and number of monitoring locations (near entry points, average residence time, high TTHM, high HAA5) by source water type and population size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables in §141.601(b)(1) specify required total samples per monitoring period and distribution among location types (different breakouts for subpart H and ground water and for population size categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample location distribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Take samples at locations other than existing subpart L compliance locations and distribute monitoring locations throughout the distribution system; if entry points are fewer or greater than specified, follow replacement rules (replace excess entry point samples equally at high TTHM and HAA5 locations or prioritize highest-flow entry points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are fewer entry points than entry-point monitoring locations, replace excess equally at high TTHM and HAA5 locations; if more entry points, sample those with highest annual flows. Monitoring under §141.601 cannot be reduced under §141.29 and State may not reduce monitoring under §142.16(m).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDSE report required contents (standard monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDSE report must include all TTHM and HAA5 analytical results from subpart L compliance monitoring and all standard monitoring conducted during the IDSE period as individual analytical results and LRAAs in a tabular/spreadsheet format acceptable to the State; if changed from the submitted plan, include a schematic, population and system type, explanation of deviations, recommended subpart V monitoring locations justified per §141.605, and retention/make-available provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain the complete IDSE report for 10 years after submission; if the State modifies recommended monitoring, keep a copy of the State's notification for 10 years; make the IDSE report and State notifications available for State or public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: System specific study — use of existing monitoring results (minimums)
rubrics_metrics.description: A system specific study may be based on previously collected monitoring results that meet criteria: samples collected/analyzed per §141.131 no earlier than 5 years prior; monitoring locations and frequency must meet minimum sample requirements in the §141.602(a)(1)(i)(B) table (number of locations and number of samples by system type/population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If previously collected data fully meet sample number requirements, submit them and certify completeness and representativeness; include distribution schematic, population and system type; retain copy as required. If State rejects data, conduct additional monitoring or standard monitoring per State-approved schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: System specific study — modeling minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If relying on an extended-period hydraulic model, it must simulate 24-hour demand variation and represent specified coverage: 75% pipe volume; 50% pipe length; all pressure zones; all 12-inch+ pipes; 8-inch+ pipes that connect pressure zones/influence zones/storage/major demand areas/pumps/control valves or are significant conveyors; 6-inch+ pipes connecting remote areas; all storage facilities, active pump stations with controls, and active control valves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model must be calibrated or have calibration plans for the current configuration during high TTHM formation periods; all calibration must be completed no later than 12 months after plan submission. See §141.602(a)(2)(i) for the full list of representational requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: System specific study — modeling reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A system specific study plan using modeling must include tabular data demonstrating model meets representation requirements, description of calibration activities and calibration graphs (predicted vs measured tank levels for highest residence time storage in each pressure zone), a time series graph of residence time for longest residence storage, model output of preliminary 24-hour average residence time predictions, planned timing/number of samples representative of distribution, schematic, population and system type, and a description of how requirements will be completed within 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include model outputs showing preliminary 24-hour average residence times and ensure samples planned are no less than would be required under standard monitoring; retain complete plan for as long as IDSE report retention requires. If model does not meet requirements, correct deficiencies or conduct standard monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDSE report required contents (system specific study/modeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system specific study was used, IDSE report must include all TTHM and HAA5 analytical results from subpart L and system specific study monitoring in tabular/spreadsheet form; if modeling was used include final modeling elements and 24-hour time series residence time graphs for each selected subpart V location; recommend and justify subpart V monitoring locations per §141.605; explain deviations; provide the analytical/modeling basis for location selection; retain report for 10 years and make available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDSE report may be submitted in lieu of the system specific study plan if all required information is available at the plan due date. Retention and public/state access requirements apply (10 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: 40/30 certification eligibility and certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems are eligible for 40/30 certification if they had no TTHM or HAA5 monitoring violations under subpart L and no individual sample exceeded 0.040 mg/L for TTHM or 0.030 mg/L for HAA5 during an eight consecutive calendar quarter period beginning no earlier than specified dates; must certify to State that every individual compliance sample in the period met those thresholds and there were no violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If certification is due, base eligibility on eight consecutive quarters beginning no earlier than specified dates in §141.603(a); State may require compliance monitoring results, schematics, or recommended subpart V locations; State may still require standard monitoring or system specific study despite certification; retain certification and underlying data for 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Very small system waiver conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving fewer than 500 people that have taken TTHM and HAA5 samples under subpart L are not required to comply with subpart U unless the State notifies them to conduct standard monitoring or a system specific study; systems that have not taken required samples or are notified by the State must conduct standard monitoring or a system specific study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver eligibility depends on prior sampling under subpart L and State notification. If required by State, small systems must perform standard monitoring or a system specific study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart V compliance monitoring location selection and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: IDSE report must recommend and justify subpart V compliance monitoring locations and timing for TTHM and HAA5, based on criteria and a protocol that selects locations by ranking LRAAs, subpart L average residence time locations, and other priorities in a specified sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the number of monitoring locations per the population/source table in §141.605(b); distribute locations throughout the system to the extent possible. Follow the stepwise protocol in §141.605(c)(1)–(8) to choose locations (e.g., highest TTHM LRAA not previously selected, highest HAA5 LRAA, existing subpart L max residence time with highest HAA5 LRAA, etc.). Repeat protocol if >8 locations required. If insufficient subpart L data, skip specified provisions and repeat as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart V — alternate location recommendation and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: You may recommend alternate monitoring locations if you include a rationale; if the State approves, monitor at those locations. The recommended schedule must include monitoring during the peak historical month for DBP concentrations unless State approves another month; quarterly-monitoring systems must schedule monitoring at regular 90-day (or fewer) intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate locations require State approval. Once the peak historical month is identified, quarterly systems must conduct monitoring every 90 days or less and conduct monitoring in the peak month unless State approval otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart V general applicability and compliance dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart V establishes national primary drinking water regulations for achieving compliance with LRAA-based MCLs for TTHM and HAA5, and MRDLs for chlorine/chloramine for certain consecutive systems; applicability covers community and nontransient noncommunity systems using disinfectants other than UV. Compliance dates are specified by system type/population with provisions for State-granted extensions for capital improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must begin monitoring as specified in the schedule table in §141.620(c). If quarterly monitoring is required, begin in first full calendar quarter that includes the compliance date; if monitoring is less than quarterly, begin monitoring in the month recommended by the IDSE or subpart V monitoring plan no later than 12 months after the compliance date. States may grant up to 24 additional months for capital improvement needs.
